tasks.title: Extract the extension-to-language mapping into a shared module
tasks.detail:
Goal: Move the file route's private extension-to-language mapping into a shared module so the browser editor highlights with exactly the same language ids the server already reports.
Files: create `lib/file-language.ts` and `lib/file-language.test.mjs`; modify `app/api/files/[...path]/route.ts` only to remove the local copies and import the module. Do not touch any other file, and do not touch the `PUT` work owned by TASK-006; this task finalises its edits to `app/api/files/[...path]/route.ts` before TASK-006 reopens that same file, and the two are serialised by `pre_request` (TASK-001 in wave 1, TASK-006 in wave 2) so the shared ownership never races.
Contract: `lib/file-language.ts` exports exactly
  export const EXT_TO_LANGUAGE: Record<string, string>
  export function getLanguage(filePath: string): string
Move the existing `EXT_TO_LANGUAGE` constant and `getLanguage` function bodies out of `app/api/files/[...path]/route.ts` **verbatim**, including the full-name special cases (`dockerfile` and `dockerfile.*` -> `"dockerfile"`, `.env` and `.env.*` -> `"bash"`, `makefile`/`gnumakefile` -> `"makefile"`) and the `EXT_TO_LANGUAGE[ext] ?? "text"` fallback. Behaviour must be byte-identical; the returned ids (`typescript`, `javascript`, `markdown`, `bash`, `text`, ...) are the contract the client depends on.
Steps:
1. Create `lib/file-language.ts` with the moved constant and function.
2. In `app/api/files/[...path]/route.ts`, delete the local `EXT_TO_LANGUAGE` and `getLanguage` and add `import { getLanguage } from "@/lib/file-language";` next to the other `@/lib` imports. Keep the import ordering style already used in that file.
3. Add `lib/file-language.test.mjs` using `node:test` + `node:assert/strict` that imports `./file-language.ts` and asserts: `getLanguage("src/a.ts") === "typescript"`, `getLanguage("a.tsx") === "typescript"`, `getLanguage("Dockerfile.dev") === "dockerfile"`, `getLanguage(".env.local") === "bash"`, `getLanguage("Makefile") === "makefile"`, `getLanguage("notes.md") === "markdown"`, `getLanguage("unknown.zzz") === "text"`.
Verify: `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/file-language.test.mjs` passes and `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` reports no errors.
Done when: `app/api/files/[...path]/route.ts` contains no `EXT_TO_LANGUAGE` definition and no local `getLanguage`, the new test passes, and `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

tasks.title: Add mode-preserving atomic write and pure edit-validation helpers
tasks.detail:
Goal: Provide the pure, unit-tested server primitives that the `PUT` file route needs: an atomic write that keeps the target's permission bits, a revision token, and body validation with a fixed error precedence.
Files: extend `lib/atomic-file.ts`; create `lib/file-edit.ts` and `lib/file-edit.test.mjs`. Do not modify `writePrivateFileAtomicSync` or any other existing export.
Contract: add to `lib/atomic-file.ts`
  export function writeFileAtomicSync(path: string, contents: string, mode: number): void
It writes to a temp file `.{basename}-{randomUUID()}.tmp` in the same directory as `path` using `writeFileSync(tempPath, contents, { encoding: "utf8", flag: "wx", mode, flush: true })`, then `renameSync(tempPath, path)`. In `finally` it unlinks the temp path, ignoring `ENOENT`, and rethrows a non-`ENOENT` unlink error only when the main operation did not already fail (same shape as `writePrivateFileAtomicSync`). The temp file must stay in the target's directory so the `fs.watch` on that directory sees the rename.
Create `lib/file-edit.ts` exporting exactly:
  export const MAX_FILE_EDIT_BYTES = 1024 * 1024;
  export const FILE_EDIT_TOO_LARGE_ERROR = "File is too large to edit";
  export function fileRevision(stat: { mtimeMs: number; size: number; ino: number }): string;
  export type FileEditValidation = { ok: true; content: string } | { ok: false; status: number; error: string };
  export function validateFileEditInput(body: unknown, current: { size: number; revision: string }): FileEditValidation;
Rules, in this exact order:
1. `current.size > TEXT_PREVIEW_MAX_BYTES` (import from `@/lib/file-types`) -> `{ ok: false, status: 413, error: FILE_EDIT_TOO_LARGE_ERROR }`. This is checked first so a file that was never fully loaded reports its real problem instead of a conflict.
2. `body` is not a non-null object, or `content` is not a string, or `baseRevision` is not a string -> `{ ok: false, status: 400, error: "Expected { content, baseRevision }" }`.
3. `Buffer.byteLength(content, "utf8") > MAX_FILE_EDIT_BYTES` -> `{ ok: false, status: 413, error: FILE_EDIT_TOO_LARGE_ERROR }`.
4. `content.includes("\u0000")` -> `{ ok: false, status: 415, error: "Binary files cannot be edited" }`.
5. `baseRevision !== current.revision` -> `{ ok: false, status: 409, error: "File changed on disk" }`.
6. otherwise `{ ok: true, content }`.
`fileRevision` returns `` `${Math.trunc(stat.mtimeMs)}:${stat.size}:${stat.ino}` ``.
Steps:
1. Add `writeFileAtomicSync` to `lib/atomic-file.ts`.
2. Create `lib/file-edit.ts` as specified.
3. Create `lib/file-edit.test.mjs` covering: every branch above (400 x3 shapes, 409, 413 twice, 415, ok), the exact `fileRevision` string for a synthetic stat, and a real round trip in `mkdtemp` using `writeFileAtomicSync(file, "hello\n", 0o644)` asserting the content, `(statSync(file).mode & 0o777) === 0o644`, and that `readdirSync(dir)` contains only the written file (no leftover `.tmp`).
Verify: `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/file-edit.test.mjs` passes and `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` is clean.
Done when: all branches are asserted, the round trip preserves mode and leaks no temp file, and existing users of `lib/atomic-file.ts` are unaffected.

tasks.title: Install CodeMirror 6 and add the lazy language loader
tasks.detail:
Goal: Add the CodeMirror 6 runtime and a dynamic language loader so the editor highlights only the languages it has a package for, and loads nothing for the rest.
Files: `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `lib/code-languages.ts`, `lib/code-languages.test.mjs`. This task is the only owner of `package.json` and the lockfile.
Contract: install with caret ranges exactly these packages (versions verified on the registry on 2026-10-02): `@codemirror/state@^6.7.6`, `@codemirror/view@^6.43.13`, `@codemirror/commands@^6.11.1`, `@codemirror/language@^6.12.4`, `@codemirror/search@^6.7.2`, `@codemirror/lang-javascript@^6.2.5`, `@codemirror/lang-json@^6.0.2`, `@codemirror/lang-markdown@^6.5.2`, `@codemirror/lang-html@^6.4.12`, `@codemirror/lang-css@^6.3.1`, `@codemirror/lang-python@^6.2.1`, `@codemirror/lang-rust@^6.0.2`, `@codemirror/lang-cpp@^6.0.3`, `@codemirror/lang-java@^6.0.2`, `@codemirror/lang-sql@^6.10.0`, `@codemirror/lang-yaml@^6.1.3`, `@codemirror/lang-xml@^6.1.0`, `@codemirror/lang-go@^6.0.1`, `@codemirror/lang-php@^6.0.2`. Use `npm install <pkg>@^<ver> ...` so npm writes the caret ranges; do not add any other dependency and do not use `--save-exact`.
`lib/code-languages.ts` exports exactly:
  export async function loadLanguageExtension(language: string): Promise<Extension | null>;
`Extension` is imported as a **type only** from `@codemirror/state`. The mapping, keyed by the server's `getLanguage()` ids, uses dynamic `import()` inside the function (never a static top-level import of a language package):
  "typescript" and "javascript" -> `javascript({ typescript: true, jsx: true })` from `@codemirror/lang-javascript`
  "json" -> `json()`, "markdown" -> `markdown()`, "html" -> `html()`, "css" -> `css()`, "python" -> `python()`, "rust" -> `rust()`, "cpp" and "c" -> `cpp()`, "java" -> `java()`, "sql" -> `sql()`, "yaml" -> `yaml()`, "xml" -> `xml()`, "go" -> `go()`, "php" -> `php()`
Everything else (`text`, `bash`, `toml`, `graphql`, `dockerfile`, `makefile`, `hcl`, `kotlin`, `swift`, `csharp`) returns `null`.
Steps:
1. Run the `npm install` above from the repository root. This is a running `next dev` checkout; after install, do not restart the server and do not run `next build`.
2. Create `lib/code-languages.ts` as specified.
3. Create `lib/code-languages.test.mjs` asserting `await loadLanguageExtension("typescript") !== null`, `await loadLanguageExtension("markdown") !== null`, `await loadLanguageExtension("text") === null`, `await loadLanguageExtension("bash") === null`, and that the source contains no static `from "@codemirror/lang-` import (read the file and assert with a regex) so lazy loading cannot silently regress.
Verify: `npm ls @codemirror/state @codemirror/view` resolves without missing/peer errors, `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/code-languages.test.mjs` passes, and `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` is clean.
Done when: the packages are in `dependencies`, the loader resolves mapped ids and returns `null` for unmapped ones, and all language imports are dynamic.

tasks.title: Add the file-editor i18n keys to all three locales
tasks.detail:
Goal: Every user-facing string the editor adds must exist in all three locale files before any consumer task references it.
Files: `lib/i18n/messages/en.ts`, `lib/i18n/messages/zh-CN.ts`, `lib/i18n/messages/zh-TW.ts`. These files are hotspots; no other task in this plan may touch them.
Contract: add these exact keys with the given English values, placed next to the existing `i18n.fileViewMode` / `i18n.enableWrap` block in each file so the file-viewer strings stay together:
  "i18n.edit": "Edit"
  "i18n.saveFile": "Save file"
  "i18n.unsavedChanges": "Unsaved changes"
  "i18n.discardUnsavedChanges": "Discard unsaved changes?"
  "i18n.fileChangedOnDisk": "File changed on disk"
  "i18n.reloadFromDisk": "Reload from disk"
  "i18n.overwrite": "Overwrite"
  "i18n.externalChangeDetected": "This file changed on disk. Reloading would discard your unsaved edits."
  "i18n.saveFailed": "Could not save the file"
  "i18n.fileTooLargeToEdit": "This file is too large to edit"
Reuse the existing `i18n.save` ("Save"), `i18n.saving` ("Saving…"), `i18n.saved` ("Saved"), and `i18n.cancel` keys in the UI; do not add duplicates of them. Every new key must have a named consumer inside this plan: `i18n.unsavedChanges` is the dirty-indicator label in TASK-008 step 9 and `i18n.fileTooLargeToEdit` is the disabled Edit-button tooltip in TASK-008 step 1, so neither may be dropped or left unused. `zh-CN.ts` and `zh-TW.ts` get accurate Simplified and Traditional Chinese translations of the same keys; the key names must match `en.ts` exactly.
Steps:
1. Add the ten keys to `lib/i18n/messages/en.ts` in the file-viewer block.
2. Add the same ten keys to `lib/i18n/messages/zh-CN.ts` and `lib/i18n/messages/zh-TW.ts` at the equivalent position with Chinese values.
3. Confirm no key is duplicated inside a file.
Verify: `node --experimental-strip-types --test lib/i18n/registry.test.mjs lib/i18n/format.test.mjs` passes; `node -e` a quick script or `grep -c` to confirm each of the ten keys appears exactly once per locale file; `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` is clean.
Done when: all three locales contain the ten new keys with no duplicate and no missing key, and the i18n tests pass.

tasks.title: Add PUT file writing and the read revision token
tasks.detail:
Goal: Serve atomic, authorized file writes and expose the revision token the client must send back, so a save can be rejected when the file moved on underneath it.
Files: `app/api/files/[...path]/route.ts` and a new `app/api/files/write-route.test.mjs`. Do not touch the route test files that already exist (`stream-route.test.mjs`, `watch-route.test.mjs`).
Contract: first, add the revision token to the text `GET` read response so the client has a base: the existing `if (type === "read")` text branch currently returns `{ ...chunk, language, size: stat.size }`; it must additionally return `revision: fileRevision(stat)`. Binary branches (`imageMime`/`audioMime`/`videoMime`/`documentMime` via `streamFile`) are unchanged.
Then add to the same file:
  export async function PUT(request: NextRequest, { params }: { params: Promise<{ path: string[] }> })
`PUT` ignores the `type` query parameter (the client appends `?type=write`, which must not cause an error). Exact order of guards:
1. `if (!isApiRequestAllowed(request))` -> `NextResponse.json({ error: "Untrusted API request" }, { status: 403 })`.
2. `if (!hasJsonContentType(request))` -> `{ error: "Expected application/json" }`, `415`.
3. `const filePath = filePathFromApiSegments(segments)`.
4. `const allowedRoots = await getAllowedFileRoots();` require `isFilePathAllowed(filePath, allowedRoots)` and then `isExistingFilePathAllowed(filePath, allowedRoots)` (realpath containment); otherwise `{ error: "Access denied" }`, `403`. Never use `isFilePathReferencedBySession` on this path.
5. `let lstat: fs.Stats; try { lstat = fs.lstatSync(filePath); } catch { return 404 { error: "Not found" } }`. If `lstat.isSymbolicLink()` -> `400 { error: "Cannot write through a symbolic link" }`. If `!lstat.isFile()` -> `400 { error: "Not a file" }`.
6. `const stat = fs.statSync(filePath)` and `const revision = fileRevision(stat)`.
7. `const body = await request.json().catch(() => null);` then `const validated = validateFileEditInput(body, { size: stat.size, revision });` and on `!validated.ok` return `NextResponse.json({ error: validated.error }, { status: validated.status })`.
8. `writeFileAtomicSync(filePath, validated.content, stat.mode & 0o777);`
9. Re-`stat` and return `NextResponse.json({ revision: fileRevision(next), size: next.size, mtime: next.mtime.toISOString() })`.
Wrap the body in the same `try/catch` shape as `POST` so unexpected errors become `500 { error }`. New imports: `fileRevision`, `validateFileEditInput` from `@/lib/file-edit`; `writeFileAtomicSync` from `@/lib/atomic-file`; `hasJsonContentType` from `@/lib/request-security`.
Steps:
1. Add `revision` to the text `read` response.
2. Add the `PUT` handler exactly as specified, placed after `POST` and before `GET` or at the end of the file — match the file's existing ordering style.
3. Write `app/api/files/write-route.test.mjs` following `watch-route.test.mjs`: read `./[...path]/route.ts`, slice the `PUT` block, and assert it calls `isApiRequestAllowed`, `hasJsonContentType`, `lstatSync` with an `isSymbolicLink()` refusal, `isExistingFilePathAllowed`, `validateFileEditInput`, `writeFileAtomicSync` with `stat.mode & 0o777`, and returns `revision: fileRevision(next)`; also assert the `read` branch contains `revision: fileRevision(stat)` and that the `PUT` signature exists. Plus one structural assertion that the origin check appears before the content-type check, and both before any `fs` call.
Verify: `node --experimental-strip-types --test "app/api/files/write-route.test.mjs"` passes, the pre-existing `node --experimental-strip-types --test "app/api/files/*.test.mjs"` still passes, and `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` is clean.
Done when: `PUT` is reachable, all guards are in the specified order, the read response carries `revision`, and the assertions pass.
